{"parse":{"title":"List of Billboard 200 number-one albums of 2007","pageid":8622357,"redirects":[],"wikitext":"{{short description|None}}\n\nThe highest-selling albums and [[extended play|EPs]] in the United States are ranked in the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]], published by ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine. The data are compiled by [[Nielsen Soundscan]] based on each album's weekly physical and [[digital distribution|digital]] sales.<ref name=\"exclusive\">{{cite magazine|first=Mitchell|last=Peters|title=Revised Chart Policy Lands Eagles At No. 1|url=http://www.billboard.biz/bbbiz/content_display/charts/chart_alert/e3i680cdd40645913b006ab7f204ebf917b|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090419052121/http://billboard.biz/bbbiz/content_display/charts/chart_alert/e3i680cdd40645913b006ab7f204ebf917b|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 19, 2009|magazine=Billboard|date=2007-11-06| accessdate=2007-11-06}}</ref> In [[2007 in music|2007]], there were 37 albums that reached peak position, in 52 issues of the magazine.\n\n[[File:Josh Groban (Cropped).jpg|thumb|American singer-songwriter [[Josh Groban]]'s ''[[Noël (Josh Groban album)|Noël]]'' is the best-selling and the longest-running album of 2007, topping the chart for four consecutive weeks.]]\n\n''[[Noël (Josh Groban album)|Noël]]'', a [[Christmas album]] by American singer-songwriter [[Josh Groban]], was the longest-running album of 2007, topping the chart for four consecutive weeks in December. Its four-week consecutive run gained ''Noël'' the credit as the first Christmas album to have achieved the feat in the chart's 51-year history.<ref name=\"HarrisGroban\">{{cite news|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1576796/josh-grobans-noel-becomes-2007s-best-seller.jhtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120209095708/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1576796/josh-grobans-noel-becomes-2007s-best-seller.jhtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 9, 2012|title=Josh Groban's Noel Surpasses 'High School Musical 2' As 2007's Best Seller|last=Harris|first=Chris|date=2007-12-19|publisher=MTV|accessdate=2009-03-02}}</ref> Following Groban's appearance at ''[[The Oprah Winfrey Show]]'', sales of the album logged at 405,000, fueling the album to peak at number one and becoming Groban's best sales week ever. ''Noël'' is the only [[Christmas]]-themed record to have topped the ''Billboard''&nbsp;200 since American [[saxophone|saxophonist]] [[Kenny G]]'s 1994 ''[[Miracles: The Holiday Album]]''.<ref name=\"HastyGroban\">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1047006/groban-remains-no-1-becomes-07s-best-seller|title=Groban Remains No. 1, Becomes '07's Best-Seller|last=Hasty|first=Katie|date=2007-12-19|magazine=Billboard|accessdate=2009-02-01}}</ref> ''Noël'' had accumulated sales of nearly 2.8 million copies by the end of the year, becoming the best-selling album of 2007.<ref name=\"HarrisGroban\"/>\n\nCanadian singer [[Avril Lavigne]] scored her second number-one album [[The Best Damn Thing]].\n''[[High School Musical 2 (soundtrack)|High School Musical 2]]'', the soundtrack to the [[List of Disney Channel Original Movies|Disney Channel film]] of the [[High School Musical 2|same name]], spent four straight weeks at the top spot. The soundtrack's first-week sale of 615,000 copies made it one of the albums with biggest debut figures of 2007.<ref name=\"HastyHSM2\">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1049747/high-school-musical-2-blasts-in-at-no-1|title='High School Musical 2' Blasts In At No. 1|last=Hasty|first=Katie|date=2007-08-22|magazine=Billboard|accessdate=2009-02-01}}</ref> The soundtrack sold over 2.7 million units in 2008, becoming the second-best-selling album.<ref name=\"HarrisGroban\"/> ''High School Musical 2'' is one of the two [[soundtrack album]]s to have reached number one on the chart, the other being ''[[Dreamgirls: Music from the Motion Picture]]''. [[Linkin Park]]'s ''[[Minutes to Midnight (Linkin Park album)|Minutes To Midnight]]'' becomes the band's third number-one album. The album sells over 620,000 copies in its first week, becoming the third highest first week album sales for 2007. The album eventually sells over 2 million copies during the year, becoming the seventh best-selling album of the year. American singer [[Alicia Keys]]' ''[[As I Am (Alicia Keys album)|As I Am]]'' also topped the chart for four weeks, although they were non-consecutive. It debuted on the ''Billboard''&nbsp;200 for selling 742,000 copies, the highest figure achieved for a solo female artist since [[Norah Jones]]' ''[[Feels Like Home (Norah Jones album)|Feels Like Home]]'' moved one million copies in 2004.<ref name=\"CohenMegaAsIAm\">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1047254/keys-storms-chart-with-mega-selling-as-i-am|title=Keys Storms Chart With Mega-Selling 'As I Am'|last=Cohen|first=Jonathan|date=2007-11-21|magazine=Billboard|accessdate=2009-01-29}}</ref>\n\nRapper [[Kanye West]]'s ''[[Graduation (album)|Graduation]]'' took the distinction as the album with the highest sales in a week, netting over 957,000 units. It is the best sales week by any album since rapper [[50 Cent]]'s ''[[The Massacre]]'' opened with over 1.1 million copies in March 2005.<ref name=\"MayfieldHuge\">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1049182/kanye-crushes-50-cent-in-huge-album-sales-week|title=Kanye Crushes 50 Cent In Huge Album Sales Week|last=Mayfield|first=Geoff|date=2007-09-18|magazine=Billboard|accessdate=2009-02-01}}</ref> [[Rock music|Rock]] band [[The Eagles]] landed atop the chart with ''[[Long Road out of Eden]]'', which sold 711,000 copies, the band's first studio album in 30 years. Sold through retailers [[Wal-Mart]], [[Sam's Club]] and the band's web site, it marked the first time ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine allowed exclusive albums to appear on the ''Billboard''&nbsp;200.<ref name=\"HastyPast\">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1047390/eagles-fly-past-britney-to-debut-at-no-1|title=Eagles Fly Past Britney To Debut At No. 1|last=Hasty|first=Katie|date=2007-11-07|magazine=Billboard|accessdate=2012-07-08}}</ref> Rapper [[Jay-Z]] produced his 10th number-one album, ''[[American Gangster (album)|American Gangster]]'', placing him second, tying with [[Elvis Presley]], in the acts with the most number-one albums in the history of ''Billboard''&nbsp;200, only behind band [[the Beatles]] who had 19.<ref name=\"HastyLeap\">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1047319/jay-z-leapfrogs-eagles-britney-for-no-1-debut|title=Jay-Z Leapfrogs Eagles, Britney For No. 1 Debut|last=Hasty|first=Katie|date=2007-11-14|magazine=Billboard|accessdate=2009-02-01}}</ref>\n\n==Chart history==\n\n{| class=\"wikitable\" style=\"font-size:90%;\"\n|+Key\n|style=\"background-color:#FFFF99\"|{{dagger|alt=Best performing album of 2007}}\n|Indicates best performing album of 2007\n|}\n\n{| class=\"wikitable sortable plainrowheaders\" style=\"text-align: center\"\n!
